design_decisions: Raw pointer `*T` resolves to a hidden extern ADT named "*" (copy, nonportable, no fields, elements or deref), declared after all named types so their ids stay the same. A new Ty variant would have needed body/ changes to stay a copy value.
A raw pointer is allowed only in extern fn signatures and locals. Struct fields, enum payloads, effect operations, impl types and non-extern fn signatures get the new code W0116.

A long binary chain is split by the parser into hidden-local parts of 32 operators: a block with `let chain'LO.K = part` and the rest of the chain as its tail. This is the only way within my files to make flat chains unlimited, because sema (body::Lower::binary) and the interpreter recurse per operator. The value, the order of evaluation and the short-circuit are the same. The printer prints the block back as the flat chain.

Nesting: a block inside an expression no longer pays a second nesting cost, so 96 levels holds for blocks, ifs and matches too. Chain steps cost 5 (about 150 steps), measured so that the whole pipeline at the parser's maximum runs on a 1.5 MiB stack (25% margin under 2 MiB).

Effect inference bound: 10*(n+2) rounds for n user functions. On non-convergence, one more check pass reports W0706 for each function whose effects would still change, not for every function changed in the last round.
Dependency modules have no parent module: a dependency sees its own items and the prelude, not the root package.
File markers apply only to a single file. A package uses weft.toml. Flags are OR-ed in, which is enough because every flag only switches an option on.

`weft run` streams program output live in the binary (run_live). The library `run` and `weft test` keep the output, so each test's output comes before its result line. Checker diagnostics for run and test go to stderr, so stdout carries only program output.

design_decisions: Needs your decision (RT10/F2): I added the two spec rules exactly as specified. They are sound but coarse: any use or capture of a reference counts as an access to everything it points into. The probe SCRATCH/core/probes/disjoint.wf and disjoint_parent.wf are new false positives that were clean before. Examples: two tasks that capture `stats` and touch separate fields, or `print(stats.name)` while a task writes stats.count. This is the holds-based rule that the B4 proof covers, and no corpus program or design example is affected. ADR 0006 documents it, and the corpus has a clean workaround (references to the separate fields). A precise version would need a new input relation for uses of a reference's whole value.

RT1 Rc: I tracked each handle separately (a `handle.*` dependency place) instead of giving the group root an owner. Moving or dropping any handle would then invalidate every reference into the group, which gives false positives. With per-handle tracking, a new value, a move or the end of the handle the reference came through invalidates it; dropping a clone does not; group mutations still go through the group root. dep_places keeps these places out of mutations and out of the `in` checks of W0203 and W0204.

RT1 block values: a block or match-arm value that points into the block's own locals is held in a `block value` temporary across the end of the block. The spec's scope_end rule then reports it with its derivation, with the message 'the value of this block points into `v[]`, but `v` goes out of scope at the end of the block'. Function and closure bodies are not held; W0204 reports them instead.

RT1 W0204: the check covers any returned value with places in a Local root (locals, by-value parameters, temporaries), including closures that capture locals, because the interpreter captures variable cells. I did not add a check on signatures (for example an `extern` signature whose returned place is in a by-value parameter).
RT4: a by-value argument now moves when it is evaluated, not after all arguments. This matches the interpreter, so `f(v, v.len())` is now a use after move.
RT9: only compound assignment writes through a reference. Plain `=` stays a rebind, matching the interpreter's Store.

issues.description: The new round bound 10*(n+2) is too small for a monotone inference, so valid programs that converge get a false W0706 error. The doc justification (one round moves an effect one call back, a place has at most 8 steps, so 10 rounds per function are enough) is wrong: place growth and parameter rotation compound around a recursion cycle, so the inference needs about 8*P*(k-1) rounds (k functions in the cycle, P rotating reference params). Measured with analyze_with_limit(.., 100000), all of these converge with 0 W0706: one self-recursive fn with 8 params needs 41 rounds (limit 30); 4 mutually recursive fns with 4 params need 62 (limit 60); 8 fns x 3 params need 107 (limit 100); 16 fns x 4 params need 302 (limit 180). The same text is in lib.rs round_limit, ADR 0005, architecture.md and the W0706 explain text.

issues.description: The new accesses/task_reads rules are coarse, and they apply to every field path through a reference parameter, not only to a use of a reference as a value. `world.entities` and `stats.name` emit uses(world/stats) with points_into to the whole referent. So the checker now rejects separate footprints that the base commit accepted. Examples: `s.spawn(|| print(world.entities.len())); world.score += 1` gives W0405 'task reads `world`'. `s.spawn(|| stats.count += 1); print(stats.name)` in the parent gives W0405. So do two spawns that touch stats.count and stats.name, and `fork(|| stats.count += 1, || print(stats.name))`. The design states 'Tasks ... must have separate footprints', so this field-level separation is reasonable code. The implementer marked this as a decision. The rule is wider than the implementer said: it covers parameters used through fields, not only reference values. sema already records the read of a reference used as a value in name(), so the generic rule adds no soundness for value uses. It only makes the check coarse.

design_decisions: F4/HOF-internal soundness: added spec relation lends_mut(P, M) (spec/weft.dl, rules.rs, bridge, diagnose Cause::Lend, Conflict.lends, random generator). A call of a fn parameter, an unknown fn value, or an op of an outer handler lends its reference args: it invalidates references and conflicts with tasks like a mutation, but needs no signature (no W0703/W0402/W0312). Without it, a HOF holding &w.entities[0] across f(w) was unsound.

New RootKind::Arg for reference parameters of closures and handler clauses (not param_rooted). This removes the W0703 false positives on closure-parameter mutations (p3). The clause parameters get these roots, as F3 asked for 'Param root'; I gave them a kind that needs no declaration.

F4 precise path: EffectSig.lent (inferred for every body, also declared ones) records which places a body gives to each fn parameter by argument position. A closure argument's parameter mutations are rebased onto those places. Fallback for callees with no inferred body (extern, prelude): every reference argument is mutated. Direct closure calls substitute the arguments.

Function values: new module crates/weft-sema/src/body/fnval.rs. FnInfo is a closure summary, an item or a param, else unknown. if/match/re-assignment join values into a merged Summary (items, params, unknown, row, members). Function items as values delegate to call_fn (call_fn_as) with the value's types.

A closure belongs to its maker: inferred rows include escapes and muts of every closure made in the body. Returned fn values get EffectSig.ret (RetFn), so a later call of the result applies the callee's ret summary (resolved at the maker's call site).

Stored closures (struct field, payload, container, generic by-value arg, callee stores, user extern) are tracked. A post-pass applies them at every reach node: a call of an unknown value, or a non-std call with a fn-holding argument. It is flow-insensitive, so loops are covered, and it propagates through closure application nodes. EffectSig.stores records which fn params a body stores.

issues.description: A closure that captured a reference is accepted when it is wrapped in a struct literal or a tuple argument. call_fn emits call_arg only for the refs of Fn-typed arguments, so `apply_cb(Cb { f: || print(r.hp) }, world)` and `apply_pair((|| print(r.hp), 1), world)` miss W0312, although the callee clears world.entities and then runs the closure.

issues.description: Places that alias each other, given to one function value, are never checked for W0312. Inside the higher-order function, `f(w, &w.entities[0])` (or `g(|| print(r.hp), world)` with g a fn parameter) only adds lends_mut, which has no alias_conflict rule. At the caller, the closure's parameter mutations are rebased onto the places given, but no call_arg ties the other parameter's place to them. So `give_two(|x, e| { x.entities.clear(); print(e.hp) }, world)` is a use after free and is accepted. A direct closure call with the same arguments gives W0312 (f4_alias.wf line 22).

issues.description: A multi operation reached through an unknown function value inside a callee does not make the caller's call node multi. call_field(s) does `let g = s.f; g()`. I verified a git-archive snapshot of HEAD 53d49ba against base 9713ccc. Each was built in its own target directory under SCRATCH/verify/review_core/ (head_target, base_target), and the runner is Core_S2/run.sh. I did not edit the worktree.

Gates:
- cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings and cargo test --workspace all pass on HEAD.
- Random agreement also passes with PROPTEST_CASES=20000.
- weft agree holds on every probe file I wrote.
- Every tests/programs/*.wf matches its //~ markers through the CLI.
- In the new corpus files 37 to 41, no bad-case marker fires on base, and the 4 base W0703 false positives in 38 are gone.

Regressions: across all ~100 red-team, spec-review and earlier verify probes, the only diagnostic that base gives and HEAD drops is the intended removal of the W0703 false positive in p3.

Every original probe now gives the expected diagnostic at the expected line. RT17 and RT24 hold for every variant I tried.

The other findings each have unsound shapes that still escape. All are reported as major:
- RT6 and RT7: a function value re-assigned later in a loop body.
- RT7: a closure or item stored through Vec.push or another generic T parameter.
- RT7: a returned closure's returned closure (`fn() -> fn()`).
- RT7: a callback that returns a closure, which the higher-order function then calls.
- F3 with RT7: a stored closure that performs, run under the handler. apply_stored runs after the clause-parameter rebasing, so the clause's mutation is lost.
- F3: a perform whose closure argument captured a reference (no call_arg for the closure).
- F3: a clause-parameter reference held across resume (the captured-place form is caught).
- F4: an Arg-rooted place that escapes through `keep = x`.
- RT5: a closure wrapped in a struct or tuple argument.
- F4 and RT5: aliasing places given to one function value. lends_mut has no W0312 counterpart, so `give_two(|x, e| { x.entities.clear(); print(e.hp) }, world)` is accepted.
- RT13: a multi operation reached through an unknown value inside a callee is not visible to callers.

Two pre-existing general gaps share these causes and are reported as NEW:
- Reference locals re-assigned in loops.
- Reference-holding tuple and Option arguments are not call_args.

Minor:
- A stored callback's parameter mutation is coarsened to the whole argument. This adds a new false positive: W0301 and W0703 'mutates `w`' in an event-handler pattern.
- The program-wide multi test gives W0503 on with_lock.
